 Pippa Matthews, formerly Middleton, and her husband James have been ordered to remove an unauthorised car park.
 The order came after the car park was constructed on a meadow at their 145-acre country estate in Kintbury.
 West Berkshire Council made the order after the couple had the 400 square metre car park laid on their Barton Court estate, which they bought for £15.5 million in 2022, without planning consent.
 The land was previously used for grazing and haymaking and has particular significance for locals as the summer home of two heavy horses, Monty and Drummer, which pulled a barge along the nearby Kennet and Avon Canal.
 The car park was intended for anglers using the estate's fishing facilities, but residents were unhappy with the lack of consultation.
 Council documents, reported by The Times, reveal the dissatisfaction of many parishioners who found the meadow converted into a private car park.
 Planning inspectors highlighted that the development had "introduced a visually intrusive and urbanised feature into an otherwise open meadow", causing direct harm to the rural landscape.
 The construction, according to the inspectors, "eroded a measure of the open and undeveloped rural character" of the North Wessex Downs.
 READ MORE: Thames Valley Police catch driver without licence or insurance for third time 
 The estate attempted to justify the development through a retrospective planning application in November last year, arguing the car park was essential for visiting anglers, as fishing rights along the river represented "a significant income stream which supports the wider upkeep of the land".
 However, the council was unconvinced and refused permission in February.
 An appeal was lodged by the estate, but a Government-appointed inspector dismissed it in July, determining the car park's scale and engineered appearance were incompatible with its rural setting.
 The Matthews couple have been involved in previous disputes with their neighbours.
 One anonymous resident reported "a lot of ill will and residual anger" following a separate dispute over a footpath running through the estate.
 The Matthews successfully fought to stop the public from using the path, which locals said had been walked for generations.
 The couple faced accusations of using their royal connections to justify closing the path.
 However, a Government-appointed inspector ruled last month there was insufficient evidence to confirm the path had been freely used by the public, overturning its designation as a right of way.
 Further complaints about the car park centred on the removal of hedgerow to accommodate the development.
 One resident, in a written objection to the council, described being "shocked when all the fencing went up and a huge gravel area was laid at the side of this marsh in a rural area".
 The objection questioned the need for new hard standing on open land, noting, "Barton Court is a large estate, they surely have hard standing in their own premises if they so wish rather than creating a new brownfield site."
